# Handle a latest endpoint change

```bash
jbpa artifact inspect --version latest --latest-observation /var/lib/jbpa/latest-observation.json
```

Keep the observation in a private directory. LATEST_RESOLUTION_CHANGED is informational because the source is mutable. A pinned known-package hash mismatch is ARTIFACT_CHANGED and blocks. HTML/login content, authentication failure, non-DEB content, unexpected redirects and timeouts produce structured errors; do not install or invent a redirect workaround.

If latest resolves to an unknown or unqualified package, normal installation returns LATEST_VERSION_NOT_QUALIFIED. Add the exact observed pinned URL/package to the catalogue, intake metadata, run explicitly authorized regression, compare contracts, review scoped evidence and promote manually. The static aliases remain unchanged. --allow-unqualified --controlled-test is experimental only. A latest installation uses the one inspected file/hash throughout its run rather than contacting latest again after preflight.

A retained hash-keyed package can be verified without another download using `jbpa artifact verify --version 12.10 --file /var/cache/jbpa/artifacts/PACKAGE-HASH.deb`. Local bytes are copied into private staging, bounded, hashed and inspected again. This does not resolve mutable latest: --file with latest is rejected. LOCAL_FILE retrieval has no observed effective HTTP URL.
